name: NTC mill workers' relay hunger strike, Mumbai
about: Workers from National Textile Corporation mills, organised by the National Mill Mazdoor Union, began an indefinite relay hunger strike on 6 October.
demands: Payment of long-pending wages and retirement benefits.

context.question: Why are NTC mill workers on hunger strike?
context.short: The government-owned National Textile Corporation stopped production at its mills in the March 2020 COVID-19 lockdown and has not restarted. Workers say they have been paid half wages, irregularly, ever since, and are owed months of arrears.
explainer: The National Textile Corporation runs 23 mills across seven states and one union territory. Production at its mills stopped in March 2020.

In Mumbai, four NTC mills (Tata Mills, Podar Mills, India United No. 5 and Digvijay) closed during the pandemic and have not reopened. Pay was cut to half after a few months, and only a small number of workers are called in, mostly for maintenance.
Members of the National Mill Mazdoor Union began an indefinite relay hunger strike in Mumbai on 6 October 2026.
impact: The Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh says 11 months of wages are unpaid and has asked the Prime Minister to fund a restart of 12 modernised mills.
Authorities have reportedly said the dues can be cleared only after mill properties are sold.
Workers have described taking loans and drawing down their provident funds; in 2023 some reported taking home less than Rs 2,000 a month after deductions.
